experience.summary: An AI research assistant on energy access in Africa that cites a curated library of sector reports. Team of 4. Sole engineer for the first month, building the product from the frontend to the infrastructure.
highlights: Built the Next.js and TypeScript frontend, streaming answers as they are generated with inline citations that link back to the source passage.
Built retrieval in PostgreSQL with no separate vector database: pgvector semantic search (HNSW) and keyword search, merged with reciprocal rank fusion.
Built the answering service in Python (FastAPI) with no LangChain. Calls Claude via AWS Bedrock, streams inline citations, declines unsupported questions.
Built document ingestion on Redis Streams with consumer groups, parallel workers and a dead-letter stream, so large PDFs are embedded without slowing the API.
Isolated each organisation's data with PostgreSQL row-level security.

Wrote the CloudFormation stacks for three containerised services on ECS Fargate, cutting environment setup from days to under fifteen minutes. Three junior engineers set it up alone after one onboarding call.
Built a pull request review agent used by the Access to Energy and Hoppers teams. It combines two models' reviews and flags me only when they disagree. A human approves every merge.

experience.position: Full Stack Software Engineer (Contract, Part Time)
experience.summary: Event ticketing platform. Built the payment handling and the ticket reservation flow.
highlights: Built payment handling for two providers (DPO, IoTec) with idempotent webhooks and row-level locking, stopping duplicate charges.
Stopped double booking: tickets are claimed with `select_for_update`, then held with an expiry until payment succeeds or the hold lapses.
Delivered features across the Django backend, React admin panel and Flutter app, including QR ticketing with server-side validation and team permissions.

experience.summary: Promoted to Senior in March 2023. Stepped away in May 2025 to complete MSc in Data Analytics full time.
highlights: Owned three client-facing products end to end: the candidate assessment platform (the games candidates take), the recruiter portal and client analytics dashboards, built in Django, PostgreSQL and React.
Led a team of five for about two months after our manager left, alongside a full workload. Every sprint commitment was met.
Pushed back on deprecating a database table in one sprint, mapped where it was still used and proposed a staged plan, preventing a production break.
Built candidate scoring on Celery queues with RabbitMQ, and a fan-out exchange to two services with idempotent consumers.
Took over the Snowflake and dbt pipeline behind the dashboards when the data scientist left. Agreed with product and data science what counts as a completed assessment (12 of 16 games).
Fixed broken assessment games as severity one, shipping straight away and monitoring with New Relic.
Joined a two week investigation rotation, making data migrations safe with backups, undo scripts and staging runs.
Ran 15+ technical interviews against an existing rubric. Wrote onboarding documentation for systems where I was the bottleneck.
Built the assessment games candidates take, used by around 500,000 candidates a day, including accessibility accommodations (colour blindness, dyslexia font, extra time).
Fixed an N+1 query problem for a client with 120,000+ records: endpoint from 8 to 12 seconds to under 800ms by replacing a query per record with a fixed number of prefetched queries.
Automated the micro-frontend deploy on push (GitHub Actions, S3, CloudFront): manual work from about twenty minutes to under five, deployment errors from about five a quarter to none.
